explanation_short: Increasing the number of features used in the KNN model leads to a consistent improvement in both R² and MSE.  The best performance is achieved with 11 features, resulting in an R² of 0.81717 and an MSE of 0.012810.
explanation_full: Incremental feature analysis reveals that adding more features to the KNN model consistently improves its predictive performance.  The R² metric, which measures the proportion of variance explained by the model, increases as the number of features grows. Similarly, the MSE (Mean Squared Error), a measure of prediction accuracy, decreases with each additional feature. The most significant gains are observed when moving from 3 to 4 features and again from 8 to 9 features.  Ultimately, using all 11 features results in the best overall performance, achieving an R² of 0.81717 and an MSE of 0.012810. This suggests that a comprehensive set of features is crucial for accurately predicting hydrogen production.
